findings.summary: Output ports named g/ctrl/p match the isPhysicalOutputPort input-name list, so no signal branch is allocated and the scope reads a silent 0.
The test carries its own copy of validateConnection, so the real VLabWorkspace.onConnect is untested.

The default topology wires dc_voltage.p to every DUT p handle, giving cross-domain edges that bypass validation. It also uses the type thermal_reference, but the library id is thermal_ref (also in vlab_connected_benchmarks).
Param nodes=4 but only 2 ports.
VLabPort has no direction field. Signal in/out is not declared.
Ports are now Frame (6-vector across), but the legacy scalar equations compute across[0]-across[1], which is NaN on arrays. Interim: unusable with Frame blocks until WP-19a rewrites them.
Simscape port C is a Frame, but it is classified utility and so Physical. The validator rejects Frame links. Decide the classification.
Rotational/Translational, not Frame. Decide versus Simscape Multibody.
There is no distinct steam/two-phase domain, so the whole group is Fluid. Steam and liquid can be wired together without an error.
Explicit Physical ports allocate signal branches that the stub MA equations never drive.

18 inputs get spurious signal branches (switch.v, gas_flow_source.m, clarke/park/sym_comp abc...). 2 outputs and 13 unimplemented outputs get none. The assembler must use port.direction. clarke_transform and inv_sym_comp_transform are it.fails.
Strips /_[st]$/ from handles, so ports ending in _s/_t (pmsm_foc.vdc_s, iabc_s, w_s, th_s) are mis-parsed.
A step input into a PID with an active saturation clamp collapses the step to 1e-6 and exhausts the budget. Needs discontinuity/event handling.
Still swallows solver non-convergence, so GATE-02 is largely vacuous on solver failures.
Emits the domain General. The producer should emit Physical + direction.
Benchmarks 1-6 and 8-10 only assert finite state (they did before too). Add independent reference values.
Outside the band it outputs u unchanged. Simulink Dead Zone gives y = u - upper (u > upper) and y = u - lower (u < lower), so the output is continuous.
Still falls back silently and accepts alias keys. Only the pre-solve bounds protect it.
The lab used the dead param Rth=35, so the heater ran on the default R (about 5.3 kW). Now R=35, about 1.5 kW (realistic). Behaviour change in the shipped lab.
